title: Epsilon-greedy kernel curator with prefill stability probing
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: We observe variable tail latency and inconsistent token-level cost for mixed prefill/decode workloads across heterogeneous GPU fleets. Current static kernel-selection heuristics pick fast kernels for decode but often regress prefill latency for long sequence requests and cold KV-cache scenarios.

Goal: Implement a lightweight online prober (epsilon-greedy bandit) that: (1) collects short microtraces across architectures and sequence-length buckets, (2) uses a stability metric for prefill (latency variance + failure rate) to prefer conservative kernels for cold paths, and (3) decays exploration as confidence grows. The curator must be cheap (sub-microbenchmark per request path), provide deterministic fallback, and integrate with rollout controls in Console.

Scope: runtime-level prober + curator policy, signal ingestion from prefill telemetry, dashboard for per-model kernel SLOs, rollout automation (canary then global), and an eval harness for golden prompt sets. Not in scope: full model-retraining or offline global re-ranking of kernels across customers.
acceptance_criteria: Prober module integrated into runtime that performs randomized kernel probes at epsilon <= 0.05 under normal load
Per-architecture + seq-len bucket stability score computed and persisted to runtime metadata
Observed 10-30% reduction in prefill 95th percentile latency regressions for long-seqlen requests on Canary fleet compared to baseline
Deterministic fallback to default kernel family on probe failure or increased error rate
Console shows per-model kernel confidence and a single toggle to enable/rollback the curator rollout
tasks: Design prober algorithm: epsilon-greedy with decay schedule and stability metric (latency variance + error rate)
Implement lightweight microbenchmark harness for prefill paths (wear-leveling across GPUs)
Add runtime telemetry hooks: prefill start/end, kernel-id, seq-len, arch, tail-latency, error flags
Persist kernel confidence scores in metadata store and expose read API to scheduler
Integrate curator with scheduler: decision logic, safety nets, and fallback policies
Build Console dashboard: kernel SLOs, probe volume, rollout controls
Run Canary on dedicated fleet for 2 weeks, collect golden prompt evals and cost breakdowns
Write playbook for incidents and rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-11 - Priya Kapoor: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to use per-arch + 4 seq-len buckets (<64, 64-256, 256-1024, >1024). Trade-off: finer buckets give better precision but increase probe sparsity.

2026-02-18 - Diego Martinez: Prototype implemented the epsilon scheduler (epsilon=0.1 warmstart, linear decay over 72h). Observed noise on low-volume models; plan to clamp minimum probe count per bucket.

2026-02-25 - Priya Kapoor: Experiment 001 results: on A100 and A800 mix, decode kernels remain best for short seq-len but cause 1.8x variance on >1024 prefill. Switching to conservative kernel family reduced variance but increased median cost by 7%.
2026-03-02 - Diego Martinez: Updated prober to include 'stability score' = 95th_lat / median_lat + error_rate*10. Pilot Canary config created.
2026-03-08 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Integration test failures under heavy burst; root cause: probe scheduling collided with autoscaler signals. Added backpressure and probe-rate limiter.
2026-03-12 - Priya Kapoor: Canary started for 10% of dedicated fleet. Monitoring dashboard link and initial telemetry collected (see links).
notes: Decisions: start with conservative epsilon schedule; enforce probe-rate caps per-GPU; expose opt-out per-customer for Private deployments. Next milestone: automatic quantization-aware kernel grouping.
